honesty_statement: This manifest lists ONLY real, verified, publicly obtainable microscopy datasets. No synthetic microscopy images are generated or listed. Where a taxonomy class has no clean public source, this is stated explicitly rather than filled with a proxy.

resolution_target.justification: MedGemma (4B/27B multimodal) inherits Gemma 3's SigLIP-400m vision encoder, which operates at a native 896x896 input. Normalising every crop to 896x896 avoids a resolution mismatch and lets the encoder run without internal rescaling. Small native crops (e.g. NIH cells ~130x130) are aspect-preserving letterbox-padded and upscaled; large field images (BBBC041 ~1600x1200, Tryp up to 1920x1080) are aspect-preserving downscaled. Padding colour is black; padding is recorded so it is never mistaken for specimen background.

datasets.name: NIH/NLM Malaria Cell Images Dataset (segmented cells)
datasets.licence: U.S. National Library of Medicine / U.S. Government work. No explicit SPDX licence; NLM makes it publicly available for research. Treated as effectively public-domain for academic use. Citation of Rajaraman et al. 2018 requested.
datasets.citation_apa7: Rajaraman, S., Antani, S. K., Poostchi, M., Silamut, K., Hossain, M. A., Maude, R. J., Jaeger, S., & Thoma, G. R. (2018). Pre-trained convolutional neural networks as feature extractors toward improved malaria parasite detection in thin blood smear images. PeerJ, 6, e4568. https://doi.org/10.7717/peerj.4568
datasets.native_task: single-cell classification (segmented thin-smear RBC crops, ~130x130 px, Giemsa, ~100x)
datasets.checksum_note: NLM does not publish a checksum for cell_images.zip. Downloader records the SHA-256 it observes so re-runs can be verified against the first successful download.

Parasitized.note: P. falciparum thin-smear infected RBCs. Pre-training proxy class.

datasets.grouping_metadata: Patient/slide ID is encoded in the filename prefix (e.g. 'C100P61ThinF_IMG_...' -> patient C100). Used as the leakage grouping key.

datasets.name: BBBC041v1 — P. vivax (malaria) infected human blood smears
datasets.licence_caveat: NON-COMMERCIAL + ShareAlike. Fine for an academic dissertation, but any derived model/dataset redistribution must honour NC + SA. Keep BBBC041-derived crops in a separate, clearly-flagged partition so the NC constraint can be enforced downstream.
datasets.citation_apa7: Ljosa, V., Sokolnicki, K. L., & Carpenter, A. E. (2012). Annotated high-throughput microscopy image sets for validation. Nature Methods, 9(7), 637. https://doi.org/10.1038/nmeth.2083 (BBBC041 contributed by Hung, J., & Carpenter, A., Broad Bioimage Benchmark Collection).
datasets.native_task: object detection (bounding boxes) on 1000x thin smears, ~1600x1200 px

trophozoite|ring|schizont|gametocyte.note: These are P. VIVAX life stages, not falciparum. Acceptable ONLY as a genus-level Plasmodium pre-training proxy; do not treat as species-accurate. Crops must be extracted from bounding boxes before use.

datasets.grouping_metadata: Group by source image filename (image-level bounding boxes) to keep crops from one field together.

datasets.name: Tryp — microscopy images of unstained thick blood smears for trypanosome detection
datasets.citation_apa7: Anzaku, E. T., Mohammed, M. A., Ozbulak, U., Won, J., Hong, H., Krishnamoorthy, J., Van Hoecke, S., Magez, S., Van Messem, A., & De Neve, W. (2023). Tryp: A dataset of microscopy images of unstained thick blood smears for trypanosome detection. Scientific Data, 10, 716. https://doi.org/10.1038/s41597-023-02608-y
datasets.native_task: object detection on UNSTAINED THICK smears; three capture resolutions (1360x1024, 1920x1080, 720x404)

trypanosome.note: T. brucei brucei in a MOUSE model, UNSTAINED THICK smear. Strong domain shift vs Giemsa-stained cattle thin smears. Use as weakly-labelled proxy for class 1; flag domain in split metadata. Crops from bounding boxes.

datasets.grouping_metadata: Group by source frame / slide id (from figshare folder structure) to prevent tile leakage.

datasets.name: Microscopic Images of Parasites Species (Li & Zhang)
datasets.citation_apa7: Li, S., & Zhang, Y. (2020). Microscopic Images of Parasites Species (Version 2) [Data set]. Mendeley Data. https://doi.org/10.17632/38jtn4nzs6.2

Babesia.note: ONLY public source for Babesia (class 3). Species unspecified; likely human/mixed context, not cattle B. bovis/bigemina. Treat as proxy; supplement with Cherehani cattle slides.

Trypanosome.note: Giemsa-stained; complements the Tryp thick-smear source for class 1.

Plasmodium.note: Genus-level only; species not confirmed falciparum. Pre-training proxy.

Red_Blood_Cell.note: Uninfected RBC crops for the negative class.

Toxoplasma|Leishmania|Trichomonad|Leukoc.note: Out of taxonomy scope — excluded from the veterinary set (could seed an 'other/OOD' probe if needed).

datasets.grouping_metadata: No patient/slide metadata published. HIGH leakage risk: crops from one slide cannot be identified. Mitigation: treat each (species) folder as a single opaque group ('mendeley_<species>') so it lands wholly in ONE split, sacrificing cross-slide balance to avoid optimistic leakage. Documented limitation.

datasets.name: Chula-ParasiteEgg-11 (ICIP 2022 Challenge)
datasets.verified_note: Existence and contents verified. Access is GATED: IEEE DataPort account + challenge registration required; not an anonymous direct download.
datasets.licence: Distributed via IEEE DataPort competition terms; licence not stated as an open SPDX identifier on the landing page. MUST be confirmed on the IEEE DataPort page before redistribution. Academic use permitted for registered participants.
datasets.citation_apa7: Anantrasirichai, N., Chalidabhongse, T. H., Palasuwan, D., Naruenatthanaset, K., Kobchaisawat, T., Nunthanasup, N., Boonpeng, K., Ma, X., & Achim, A. (2022). ICIP 2022 challenge on parasitic egg detection and classification in microscopic images: Dataset, methods and results. In 2022 IEEE International Conference on Image Processing (ICIP). https://doi.org/10.1109/ICIP46576.2022.9897267
datasets.native_task: faecal-smear egg detection/classification, 11 human intestinal parasite egg types

ALL.note: NO clean mapping to §2. These are HUMAN intestinal parasite eggs. 'Hookworm egg' is a loose morphological analogue of strongyle-type eggs (Haemonchus, class 6) but is NOT H. contortus. Usable ONLY as a faecal-egg-morphology pre-training / domain-adaptation proxy for the faecal-float specimen type (classes 5, 6); never as ground-truth labels for Eimeria or Haemonchus.

datasets.grouping_metadata: Group by native egg-class folder; no patient metadata.

1_trypanosoma_spp.status: real images exist but domain-shifted (thick/mouse, or non-cattle); supplement with Cherehani

2_theileria_parva.status: GAP — Cherehani proprietary slides only; declared limitation

3_babesia_spp.status: single proxy source (1,173 imgs, species/host unspecified); supplement with Cherehani

4_anaplasma_spp.status: GAP — Cherehani proprietary slides only; declared limitation

5_eimeria_spp.status: GAP for labels — Cherehani slides only; Chula usable for faecal-float domain pretraining

6_haemonchus_contortus.status: GAP for labels — Cherehani slides only
